SELECT i.invoice_id, i.invoice_total, i.tax, i.delivery_fee,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(p.cost),0), 2) as lines,
       ROUND(i.invoice_total - COALESCE(SUM(p.cost),0) - i.tax - i.delivery_fee, 2) as gap

GROUP BY i.invoice_id, i.invoice_total, i.tax, i.delivery_fee
HAVING ABS(i.invoice_total - COALESCE(SUM(p.cost),0) - i.tax - i.delivery_fee) > 0.01

Yes. Four data problems, two of them already corrected in the working copy, two still open.

**Still wrong, and they distort cost**

1. **INV-010-L01, peppers, 2026-09-23.** The case is entered at $210, ten times the $21 on every other pepper line, including the delivery two days later [INV-010-L01, INV-012-L01]. That is $21/lb against a $2.10 median [snapshot: purchase prices]. The invoice header ($458.40) matches the inflated line, so this is a line error that was totaled in, not a header/line mismatch. Pepper stock still balances (unexplained −3 lb) [snapshot: stock reconciliation], which fits a price typo rather than ten times the product. Do not treat $21/lb as real.
